rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for the money charged for a service.

example.english: The charge at this clinic isn't too expensive.
example.traditional: 呢間診所嘅收費唔算貴。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 zan2 so2 ge3 sau1 fai3 m4 syun3 gwai3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice when a seller requires payment for goods or services.

example.english: This restaurant has a pretty reasonable charge.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳收費幾合理喎。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 sau1 fai3 gei2 hap6 lei5 wo3

rows.note: Use this colloquial Hong Kong verb when replenishing a battery or a device's battery.

example.english: My phone is out of battery, so I need to charge it first.
example.traditional: 我部電話冇電，要叉電先。
example.jyutping: ngo5 bou6 din6 waa2 mou5 din6 jiu3 caa1 din6 sin1

rows.note: Use this for an official criminal allegation made by the police or a court.

example.english: The police have withdrawn the charge against him.
example.traditional: 警方已經撤銷對佢嘅控罪。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 ji5 ging1 cit3 siu1 deoi3 keoi5 ge3 hung3 zeoi6

rows.note: Use this specifically for electric charge in a scientific or technical context.

example.english: This particle carries a positive charge.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 nap1 zi2 daai3 jau5 zing3 din6 ho4

rows.note: Use this when someone gives another person a duty or instruction, without necessarily implying a harsh command.

example.english: The boss put me in charge of sorting out all the documents today.
example.traditional: 老闆吩咐我負責今日整理晒啲文件。
example.jyutping: lou5 baan2 fan1 fu6 ngo5 fu6 zaak3 gam1 jat6 zing2 lei5 saai3 di1 man4 gin6

rows.note: Use this in the formal legal context of accusing someone of a crime.

example.english: The police formally charge him with arson.
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 zing3 sik1 hung3 gou3 keoi5 zung3 fo2

rows.note: Use this for the responsibility or duty that falls within someone's care.

example.english: I'm in charge of this work.
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 gung1 zok3 jau4 ngo5 fu6 zaak3
